pl-l3d2c1-d1e117.summary: States that since all of human nature in man was corrupted by vice, the Word assumed the whole, soul and flesh, to heal and sanctify the whole.
claims: The Word assumed the whole human nature, soul and flesh, to heal the whole.

pl-l3d2c1-d1e120.summary: Shows from Jerome's Exposition of the catholic faith that 'human nature' or 'humanity' means soul and flesh: there is one person of the Son in two perfect substances, deity and humanity, the latter consisting of soul and body. So when Scripture says the Son took man, humanity, or human nature, soul and body are meant.
claims: Humanity in Christ consists of soul and body.

pl-l3d2c1-d1e132.summary: Rejects the view that 'humanity', wherever Christ's humanity is mentioned, signifies not a substance but some property by which one is called man.
claims: 'Humanity' in Christ signifies a substance, not a property.

pl-l3d2c1-d1e136.summary: Supports this with John Damascene: the names deity and humanity represent substances, i.e., natures. Nature is not taken in Christ as when all men are said to have one nature, a common species predicated of many persons each composed of soul and body. In Christ there is no common species: he is one, perfect God and perfect man, from deity and humanity and in both.
claims: The names deity and humanity signify natures.
Human nature in Christ is not a common species but his own soul and body.

pl-l3d2c1-d1e148.summary: Concludes that God assumed the whole of human nature, soul and flesh with their properties or accidents, not flesh without soul or soul without reason, as heretics held, but flesh and soul with their senses.
claims: Christ assumed flesh, rational soul, and their properties.

pl-l3d2c1-d1e151.summary: Confirms with John Damascene: the Word assumed all that he planted in our nature, body, intellectual soul, and their properties; whole he assumed the whole of me, to give salvation to the whole, for what is unassumable is incurable.
claims: What is not assumed is not healed.

pl-l3d2c1.summary: Teaches that because the whole of human nature was corrupted, the Word assumed the whole, soul and flesh, to heal and sanctify the whole. Jerome shows that humanity means soul and body, so those who say 'humanity' names only a property, not a substance, err. John Damascene explains that human nature in Christ is not a common species shared by many, but the concrete nature of soul and body. God assumed soul, flesh, and their properties, not flesh without soul or soul without mind as heretics held, for what is not assumed is not healed.
claims: The Word assumed the whole human nature, soul and flesh.
'Humanity' in Christ names a substance, not a mere property.
What is not assumed is not healed.
